scripts.hook: Stop asking yourself why. Ask what.
scripts.hook_b: "Why am I like this?" is a bad question.
cards: Stop asking yourself why. Ask what.
"Why am I like this?" asks for a verdict on your whole character.
"What happened, exactly? What did I feel first?" gives you something to work with.
Research on rumination draws the same line: abstract "why" loops versus concrete "what".
It's Day 3 of the journal I made.

source.note: Watkins (2008), Psychological Bulletin 134(2): concrete vs abstract repetitive thought. Idea: Watkins · Moodius words

scripts.caption:
Day 3 of The Unexamined Self: translate one "why" question into three "what" questions and see what changes.

Evidence note in the journal: a substantial body of research, mostly correlational plus some experiments (Watkins, 2008).

scripts.hook: When someone you love goes quiet, what do you do?
scripts.hook_b: Some people chase. Some people disappear.
cards: When someone you love goes quiet, what do you do?
Some of us move toward: message again, need to fix it now.
Some of us move away: go quiet too, get busy, wait it out.
Psychologists measure these as two dials, not four boxes. Dials can move.
Idea: Fraley et al., 2015 · Moodius words
Day 17 of the journal. Comment JOURNAL for it.

source.note: Brennan, Clark & Shaver (1998); Fraley et al. (2015) JPSP 109(2): attachment as dimensions. Idea: Fraley et al. · Moodius words

scripts.hook: My journal won't fix you. Here's what it does.

cards: My journal won't fix you. Here's what it does.
It won't heal trauma or replace therapy. Nothing in a PDF can.
It gives you thirty days of looking honestly, with old philosophy and current research.
Every claim labelled: philosophy, research, or my opinion.
